label: Phase war effect text
summary: A text describing how a struggle phase affects wars, for a given character.
details: It takes two inputs: the phase and the character. Vanilla shows it in the body of the tooltip whose header is the phase's war effects (STRUGGLE_PHASE_EFFECTS_WAR_TT_HEADER), passing StrugglePhase.Self and Character.Self. That it is about wars rests on its name and that header.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The struggle phase whose effect is described.
fields.values: a struggle phase, as in StrugglePhase.Self

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character the text is shown for.

label: Has leading phase
summary: Yes or no: whether the struggle currently has a leading phase.
details: Vanilla uses it in the realm window's struggle tooltip: only when it is yes does the tooltip add the next phase, its progress and the catalyst history of the current leading phase (Struggle.GetCurrentLeadingPhase). What makes a phase the leading one is not shown by the input; the meaning rests on its name and that use.

label: Can be ended now
summary: Yes or no: whether a decision that ends the struggle is currently possible.
details: Vanilla uses it in the main HUD (hud.gui) to show an animation and a glow on the struggle's phase widget. That the decision ends the struggle rests on the name; the struggle window has its own StruggleWindow.HasPossibleEndingDecision.

label: Takes part in struggle
summary: Yes or no: whether the given character takes part in the struggle, either as an involved character or as an interloper (a character tied up in the struggle without being fully involved).
details: Vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer) and shows some parts of the struggle window only when the player does not take part. The meaning rests on the name and that use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character checked.

label: Is changing phase
summary: Yes or no: whether the struggle is currently moving from one phase to the next.
details: Vanilla shows an hourglass widget in the main HUD while it is yes, and the struggle window shows some parts only in that state and others only outside it. The meaning rests on the name and those uses.

label: Is interloper
summary: Yes or no: whether the given character is an interloper in the struggle, a character tied up in it without being fully involved.
details: Vanilla passes Character.Self in the main HUD and the character window to show or hide parts of them. The meaning rests on the name and those uses; Struggle.IsInvolvedCharacter checks the other kind of participant.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character checked.

label: Is involved
summary: Yes or no: whether the given character is one of the struggle's involved characters, the ones the struggle's region treats as a natural part of it.
details: Vanilla passes Character.Self in the main HUD, showing some parts when it is yes and others when it is not, and GetPlayer in the struggle window's phase list. The game's concept text calls involved characters a natural and integral part of the struggle for the people of its region; the exact rule is not shown by the input.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character checked.

label: Struggle as script scope
summary: The struggle turned into a script scope, so that script-side functions such as ScriptValue can be used on it.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. On other types it is written like GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('...') to read a script value; those lines are only a hint for how it works here.

label: Struggle itself
summary: The struggle itself, to pass it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument, for example to GetPlayer.GetStruggleInvolvementType( Struggle.Self ) for the text that says how the player takes part, and to IsStrugglePriority for the show-in-top-bar button. The game documents no return type.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the struggle involvement window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the struggle involvement window (the window listing who takes part in a struggle).
details: Vanilla calls it from the window's close button.

label: Participant list
summary: The list of characters the struggle involvement window shows.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data for the window's character list. Which characters it holds depends on the participant filter (all, involved, interlopers), going by the window's filter buttons. The game documents no return type.

label: Involved cultures
summary: The cultures involved in the struggle, as a list for the struggle involvement window.
details: Vanilla fills the window's culture tab with it and shows their count with GetDataModelSize.

label: Involved faiths
summary: The faiths involved in the struggle, as a list for the struggle involvement window.
details: Vanilla fills the window's faith tab with it and shows their count with GetDataModelSize.

label: Number of participants
summary: The number of participants in the struggle, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the label of the participants tab in the struggle involvement window.

label: Shown struggle
summary: The struggle the struggle involvement window is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context, so the window's parts can read the struggle's own functions. The game documents no return type.

label: Showing all participants
summary: Yes or no: whether the struggle involvement window's participant filter is set to everyone.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the "all" filter button as pressed; StruggleInvolvementWindow.SetShowAllParticipants sets that filter.

label: Showing cultures tab
summary: Yes or no: whether the struggle involvement window shows its cultures tab.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the cultures tab button as pressed and to show the culture list only then. StruggleInvolvementWindow.SetShowCultures switches to it.

label: Showing faiths tab
summary: Yes or no: whether the struggle involvement window shows its faiths tab.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the faiths tab button as pressed and to show the faith list only then. StruggleInvolvementWindow.SetShowFaiths switches to it.

label: Showing interlopers
summary: Yes or no: whether the struggle involvement window's participant filter is set to interlopers (characters tied up in the struggle without being fully involved).
details: Vanilla uses it to show the interloper filter button as pressed; StruggleInvolvementWindow.SetShowInterloperParticipants sets that filter.

label: Showing involved
summary: Yes or no: whether the struggle involvement window's participant filter is set to involved characters.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the involved filter button as pressed; StruggleInvolvementWindow.SetShowInvolvedParticipants sets that filter.

label: Showing participants tab
summary: Yes or no: whether the struggle involvement window shows its participants tab.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the participants tab button as pressed and to show that tab's content only then. StruggleInvolvementWindow.SetShowParticipants switches to it.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the struggle involvement window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Show all participants
summary: Sets the struggle involvement window's participant filter to everyone.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "all" filter button (text STRUGGLE_FILTER_PARTICIPANTS_ALL).

label: Show cultures tab
summary: Switches the struggle involvement window to its cultures tab.
details: Vanilla calls it from the tab button labelled with the cultures game concept.

label: Show faiths tab
summary: Switches the struggle involvement window to its faiths tab.
details: Vanilla calls it from the tab button labelled with the faiths game concept.

label: Show interlopers
summary: Sets the struggle involvement window's participant filter to interlopers only.
details: Vanilla calls it from the interloper filter button (text STRUGGLE_FILTER_PARTICIPANTS_INTERLOPER).

label: Show involved
summary: Sets the struggle involvement window's participant filter to involved characters only.
details: Vanilla calls it from the involved filter button (text STRUGGLE_FILTER_PARTICIPANTS_INVOLVED).

label: Show participants tab
summary: Switches the struggle involvement window to its participants tab.
details: Vanilla calls it from the tab button labelled STRUGGLE_PARTICIPANTS.

label: Access phase itself
summary: A function on a struggle phase that, going by its name, hands back the phase itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Phase background
summary: Going by its name, the background picture of a struggle phase.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. GetBackground on other types (bookmarks, activities) gives a texture for the interface; that is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Phase detail background
summary: The detail background picture of a struggle phase.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the struggle window. StrugglePhase.HasDetailBackground likely tells whether the phase has one, going by its name.

label: Ending decisions
summary: The decisions that can end the struggle in this phase, as a list.
details: Vanilla lists them in the phase tooltip and shows that part only when the list is not empty. That they end the struggle rests on the name.

label: Phase icon
summary: The icon of a struggle phase.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the struggle window and in the phase tooltip.

label: Phase name
summary: The name of a struggle phase, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in struggle tooltips, for example "Current Phase: ..." and the line saying when the next phase will start. Going by its name, StrugglePhase.GetNameNoTooltip is the same name without a hover tooltip, so this one probably has one.

label: Phase name (no tooltip)
summary: The name of a struggle phase as plain text, without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in headers, for example "Catalysts towards ..." and the ending decisions header.

label: Phase's struggle
summary: The struggle this phase belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the phase tooltip, so the tooltip can read the struggle's own functions.

label: Has background
summary: A function on a struggle phase that, going by its name, tells whether the phase has a background picture.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents no return type.

label: Has detail background
summary: A function on a struggle phase that, going by its name, tells whether the phase has a detail background picture.
details: Vanilla never uses it; StrugglePhase.GetDetailBackground gives that picture. The game documents no return type.

label: Has icon
summary: A function on a struggle phase that, going by its name, tells whether the phase has an icon.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; HasIcon on other types (laws, situation phases) is used to hide an icon that is missing, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Shows content part
summary: Yes or no: whether a given part of the phase's widget is shown for this phase.
details: Vanilla passes define values from NStruggle (ENDING_PHASE_WIDGET_CONTENT, POINT_BASED_PHASE_WIDGET_CONTENT, TIME_BASED_PHASE_WIDGET_CONTENT) to pick the matching layout in the struggle window. The meaning rests on the name and those uses.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Which content part is asked about.
fields.values: a define value, as in GetDefine( 'NStruggle', 'ENDING_PHASE_WIDGET_CONTENT' )

label: Is valid
summary: Yes or no: whether there is a struggle phase here at all.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. IsValid on other types (for example GetGovernment.IsValid) is used to check that something exists before showing it; that is only a hint.

label: Phase itself
summary: The struggle phase itself, to pass it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument, for example to Struggle.GetPhaseValue( StrugglePhase.Self ) for a phase's progress. The game documents no return type.

label: Access type itself
summary: A function on a struggle type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Struggle group type
summary: A function on a struggle type (a kind of struggle defined in the game files) that, going by its name, gives the group it belongs to.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. GetGroupType on doctrine and activity groups is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Header background
summary: Going by its name, the header background picture of a struggle type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; ActivityType.GetHeaderBackground is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Struggle type icon
summary: Going by its name, the icon of a struggle type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetIcon on other types gives an interface texture, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Struggle illustration
summary: Going by its name, the illustration (a large picture) of a struggle type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetIllustration on other types gives a picture for the interface, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Struggle type name
summary: The name of a struggle type, as text.
details: Vanilla's trigger texts use it to say which type a struggle is or is not, as in "Type of (struggle) is (type)".

label: Has header background
summary: A function on a struggle type that, going by its name, tells whether the type has a header background picture.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents no return type.

label: Has icon
summary: A function on a struggle type that, going by its name, tells whether the type has an icon.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; HasIcon on other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Struggle type itself
summary: A function on a struggle type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the struggle window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the struggle window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the window's close button.

label: End struggle
summary: A function on the struggle window that, going by its name, ends the struggle.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so what it does exactly is unknown. The game documents nothing more.

label: Catalysts of chosen phase
summary: The catalysts (actions that push the struggle towards a phase) for the phase picked in the struggle window, as a list.
details: Vanilla fills a list in the struggle window with it. The phase is the one chosen with StruggleWindow.SetSelectedPhase. The game documents no return type.

label: Ending decisions
summary: The decisions that can end the struggle, as a list for the struggle window.
details: Vanilla only counts it (GetDataModelSize) to pick a layout: one for a single decision, another for two or more. That they end the struggle rests on the name.

label: Ending phases
summary: Going by its name, the struggle's ending phases, as a list for the struggle window.
details: Vanilla fills a list with it and shows that part only when it has at least one entry; it also counts it when choosing the ending button's label. What counts as an ending phase is not shown by the input.

label: Next phases
summary: The phases the struggle can move to next, as a list for the struggle window.
details: Vanilla fills a list in the struggle window with it. The meaning rests on the name and that use. The game documents no return type.

label: Chosen phase
summary: The struggle phase picked in the struggle window.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as "View ... Ending effects" and to count how often a catalyst was completed for that phase. StruggleWindow.SetSelectedPhase picks it.

label: Shown struggle
summary: The struggle the struggle window is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context, reads its current phase (GetCurrentPhase) and shows its name.

label: Top decision
summary: Going by its name, the first or main ending decision of the struggle, shown in the struggle window.
details: Vanilla gives it to a decision tooltip when there is at most one ending decision. The game documents no return type.

label: Can be ended now
summary: Yes or no: whether a decision that ends the struggle is currently possible, as the struggle window sees it.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the struggle window and to start animations. That the decision ends the struggle rests on the name; Struggle.HasPossibleEndingDecision is the same check on the struggle.

label: Pick ending decision
summary: Called when the player clicks one of the struggle's ending decisions in the struggle window.
details: Vanilla passes the clicked decision (Decision.Self). What follows the click (opening or taking the decision) is not shown by the input.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The decision clicked.

label: Click single decision
summary: A function of the struggle window that, going by its name, handles a click on its single ending decision.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the struggle window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Choose phase
summary: Picks a struggle phase in the struggle window, to show its details.
details: Vanilla calls it when a phase is clicked, passing StrugglePhase.Self. StruggleWindow.GetSelectedPhase reads the choice back.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The phase to pick.
fields.values: a struggle phase, as in StrugglePhase.Self

label: Access contract itself
summary: A function on a subject contract that, going by its name, hands back the contract itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Administration type
summary: The short name of the administration type in a subject contract, for administrative realms.
details: Vanilla reaches it as GetVassalContract.GetAdminDivisionShortName (the vassal contract of a character) in the administration window and the map mode "Administration: ...". Those lines go through another function, so this rests on them and the name.

label: Administration type icon
summary: A text icon for the administration type in a subject contract, for administrative realms.
details: Vanilla reaches it as GetVassalContract.GetAdminDivisionTextIcon, for example in the governorship tooltip. Those lines go through another function, so this rests on them and the name.

label: Barter goods share for liege
summary: Going by its name, the share of the subject's barter goods that goes to the liege under this contract, as a fraction.
details: Vanilla shows it as a progress bar in the window for changing a vassal's contract.

label: Cease tribute chance
summary: The yearly chance that a tributary stops paying tribute, as a fraction shown as a percentage.
details: Vanilla shows it in the realm window tooltip "Yearly chance of ceasing tributary payments", followed by SubjectContract.GetCeasePayingTributeChanceDesc.

label: Cease tribute chance reasons
summary: A text explaining the yearly chance that a tributary stops paying tribute.
details: Vanilla puts it below the chance itself in the realm window tooltip. That it breaks the chance down into reasons rests on its name and place.

label: Cease tribute chance label
summary: A short text for the chance that a tributary stops paying tribute, shown after "Cease Tribute Chance:".
details: Vanilla shows it in the realm window. Whether it is a number or a word is not shown by the input.

label: Contract group
summary: The group the subject contract belongs to, such as a feudal or clan vassal contract or a tributary contract.
details: Vanilla shows its name in texts like "... Contract" and in the tributary relation frame, and uses it as data context in the admin vassal details. The examples come from SubjectContractGroup.IsType uses. The game documents no return type.

label: Herd share for liege
summary: Going by its name, the share of the subject's herd that goes to the liege under this contract, as a fraction.
details: Vanilla shows it as a progress bar in the window for changing a vassal's contract and in a shared progress bar.

label: Levy share for liege
summary: Going by its name, the share of the subject's levies (troops) that goes to the liege under this contract, as a fraction.
details: Vanilla shows it as a progress bar in the window for changing a vassal's contract and in a shared progress bar.

label: Contract's liege
summary: The liege (the higher ruler) in the subject contract.
details: Vanilla uses it in the contract's liege signature and in the notice that the liege is not the rightful liege. For a tributary contract this side is the suzerain, going by those texts. The game documents no return type.

label: Minimum levy share
summary: Going by its name, the lowest share of the subject's levies that the liege can get under this contract, as a fraction.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Minimum tax share
summary: Going by its name, the lowest share of the subject's taxes that the liege can get under this contract, as a fraction.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Obligation level
summary: Going by its name, the level set in this contract for a given obligation, as a small number.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the GetObligationLevel lines on other types are only a hint. Which input it takes is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by the name, the obligation asked about.

label: Obligation name
summary: Going by its name, the name of an obligation in this contract, as text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by the name, the obligation asked about.

label: Prestige share for liege
summary: Going by its name, the share of the subject's prestige that goes to the liege under this contract, as a fraction.

label: Is valid
summary: Yes or no: whether there is a subject contract type here at all.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. IsValid on other types is used to check that something exists before showing it; that is only a hint.

label: Contract type as script scope
summary: The contract type turned into a script scope, so that script-side functions such as ScriptValue can be used on it.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. On other types it is written like GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('...'); those lines are only a hint.

label: Contract type itself
summary: A function on a subject contract type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Uses obligation levels
summary: Going by its name, whether this contract type works with obligation levels.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the vassal list uses SubjectContract.UsesObligationLevels on the contract instead, which is only a hint.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the succession appointment window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the succession appointment window (the window for titles whose heir is appointed).
details: Vanilla calls it from the close button in window_title_appointment.gui.

label: Candidate list
summary: The list of candidates for the title, as shown in the succession appointment window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context for the window's candidate lists. The game documents no return type.

label: Candidate panel
summary: Going by its name, the part of the succession appointment window that holds the candidates.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in that window. The game documents no return type.

label: Merit pool
summary: Going by its name, the merit pool (the merit information for appointment succession) shown in the succession appointment window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context for the box holding the succession law and the merit candidate lines. The game documents no return type.

label: Merit pool text
summary: A text describing the merit pool in the succession appointment window.
details: Vanilla shows it only when SuccessionAppointmentWindow.HasMeritPoolData is yes.

label: Succession law
summary: The succession law of the title in the succession appointment window.
details: Vanilla shows its name after the succession law label. The game documents no return type.

label: Succession score breakdown
summary: The breakdown of a candidate's succession score, for the given character.
details: Vanilla passes Character.Self and uses the result as a data context in the succession appointment window. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The candidate whose score is broken down.

label: Shown title
summary: The title the succession appointment window is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and checks whether the title's holder has an administrative government (HasMechanic( 'administrative' )). The game documents no return type.

label: Top candidate
summary: A function of the succession appointment window that, going by its name, gives the leading candidate.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it checks candidates with SuccessionAppointmentWindow.IsTopCandidate instead. The game documents no return type.

label: Has merit pool data
summary: Yes or no: whether the succession appointment window has merit pool data to show.
details: Vanilla shows the merit pool description and the merit candidate description and rank lines only when it is yes.

label: Is top candidate
summary: Yes or no: whether the given character is the leading candidate in the succession appointment window.
details: Vanilla passes CharacterListItem.Self and shows different parts of the candidate row depending on the answer.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The candidate checked.
fields.values: a character list item, as in CharacterListItem.Self

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the succession appointment window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access elector itself
summary: A function on an elector in a succession election that, going by its name, hands back that elector entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Could switch to your candidate
summary: Yes or no: whether this elector could vote for the player's nominee instead of their current choice.
details: Vanilla shows a note when it is yes: the elector will vote for the player's nominee if that nominee's score is greater than their current candidate's score.

label: Elector
summary: The character who votes, from an elector entry of a succession election.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the title election window. The game documents no return type.

label: Elector's candidate
summary: The candidate this elector supports in the succession election.
details: Vanilla reads the candidate's name (GetCandidate) for texts like "Supporting ..." and the candidate's score (GetScore). The game documents no return type.

label: Vote reasons
summary: A text listing the reasons why this elector votes for their chosen candidate.
details: Vanilla shows it in the succession election widgets. That it lists reasons rests on the name and place.

label: Reasons for your candidate
summary: A text listing the reasons for and against this elector voting for the player's nominee.
details: Vanilla shows it in the succession election widgets. That it lists reasons rests on the name and place.

label: Preference for your candidate
summary: How much more or less this elector prefers the player's candidate, a whole number that can be negative.
details: Vanilla shows it with a sign after "Preference for my candidate:" in the election window and in the cardinals window.
